Endogenous and non-invasive techniques are increasingly utilized to investigate heat and mass transfer within porous beds. This study combines fixed-bed chemical reaction engineering experiments with concurrent magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) to examine temperature distributions across a powder bed reacting exothermically in gas phase. We demonstrate that MRI can detect both spatial and temporal thermal variations with high resolution, reaching a bed-average rise of approximately $14\,\textrm{K}$ above the inlet gas temperature. The observed internal thermal gradients are significantly higher than that found in an isothermal idealized simulation of the same packed bed reactor system, confirming significant heat transfer effects.

Biomolecular condensates form spontaneously within the dense cellular environment when proteins and nucleic acids demix into droplets, a process driving the organization of numerous subcellular structures. To investigate the mechanics of this organization, we utilize a coarse-grained model featuring three components to simulate the self-assembly of a two-component system where a third factor is pre-partitioned between the phases. We demonstrate that, depending on interaction parameters, the demixing process yields either homogeneous phase separation or a hierarchical structure forming nested droplets. The resulting morphology is governed by the compatibility of pairwise interactions among components; hierarchical demixing arises specifically under conditions of "all-ways-attractive" interactions, whereas simultaneous phase separation occurs with "all-ways-repulsive" scenarios. We found that condensates formed via hierarchy self-assemble more rapidly and reach smaller equilibrium sizes compared to those from general phase separation. These self-assembly rates can be tuned to match natural timescales found in eukaryotic cells. Our findings suggest that condensates and the aptamers facilitating the "all-ways-repulsive" mode may naturally co-evolve. Consequently, the ability to form via hierarchical demixing offers a promising framework for bio-artificial self-assembling systems.

This study examines the rotation of sunspots and magnetic transients at the periphery of a complex active region (AR) 11429 on the solar disk, analyzing data from 13 full-SUV images captured by SDO/AIA at three different wavelengths. By tracking bright features in these images using a simplified, visual-aided maximum entropy 2D image deconvolution "maximum entropy 2D image deconvolution" method, along with a visual aid, we demonstrate that the sunspots rotate at approximately 27 km/s at the magnetic neutral line. Simultaneously, we detect magnetic transients rotating at roughly 150 km/s at the same equatorial line. Both phenomena were documented using SDO/Magnetograms and are believed to stem from the same magnetic shear and helicity buildup, likely amplified by a magnetic flux emergence event. The observed sunspot rotation is attributed to the canonical magnetic flux cancellation occurring at the sub-photospheric level, while the faster magnetic transients represent individual magnetic flux fragments rotating towards the active region's central neutral line, likely as a result of magnetic reconnection. Both are considered critical for understanding solar flare dynamics.

This note explores a principle proposed by the second author regarding low-degree homotopy classes of maps originating from real projective spaces, with applications to verifying the Mumford conjecture (now a theorem established by Perelman). We state and discuss the weak b-principle for maps from real projective spaces targeted at complex homology spheres. Based on this principle and this application, we demonstrate the proof of the Mumford conjecture offering an alternative to Perelman's work.

This study presents a performance evaluation comparing Balancing Domain Decomposition by Constraints (BDDC) and Algebraic Multigrid (AMG) preconditioners within cardiac mechanical simulations, utilizing two finite element solvers: the Finite Element Method with Balanced Domain Decomposition and Keras-based Deep Learning frameworks. Key focus areas include numerical accuracy, computational efficiency, and scalability across diverse hardware environments. Numerical performance is assessed through convergence analyses under varying mesh densities and problem complexities. Computationally, we examine pre-and post-processing times, total simulation duration, and resource utilization, ensuring a comparative framework that evaluates the practical implementation of BDDC versus multigrid strategies in physiological biomechanics.

User-generated content is increasingly driving the success of Web 2.0 and Web 3.0 applications, a trend evident in the significant scale and growth of the data they generate. Although the temporal characteristics of this information have long been recognized as critical, datasets are rarely prepared for time-based analysis, and few studies effectively address this evolving aspect. Focusing on tag clouds from del.icio.us, this research quantifies both the reuse and time-dependency of user tags. The authors present a method for calculating tag reuse and present empirical findings showing that similar usage patterns persist across time. Additionally, we introduce a novel metric for assessing collaborative interest sharing, which further confirms that users tend to tag similar items when they collaborate. These results underscore the importance of time-sensitive designs within Social Tagging Systems.

This work details the successful generation of microacoustic waves by exciting phononic crystals at gigahertz frequencies, utilizing a micro-fabrication technique based on two-photon lithography. These periodic structures, which consist of silicon, titanium, and gold integrated with air, serve as acoustic metagratings capable of producing, manipulating, and detecting microacoustic signals. The results demonstrate the excitation of phononic crystals at gigahertz frequencies and reveal that these metagratings can operate as both functional components for detection and versatile tools for managing microacoustic energy.

This paper investigates the long-term asymptotics of the strong solutions within the 2-D FENE dumbbell model governing fluid dynamics. Specifically, it establishes that a global strong solution exhibits exponential decay as time progresses, provided the initial data possesses sufficiently small norms in the $L^{\infty}$ sense. Furthermore, it demonstrates that if the initial data is merely bounded in $L^{2}$, strong solutions remain uniformly bounded for all time; additionally, under additional assumptions of boundedness and sufficient regularity in $L^{q}$ for some $q\in[8,\pm \infty]$, it is shown that strong solutions decay exponentially over time.

The concept of the Integrated Access Backhaul (IAB) was initially envisioned within 5G New Radio (5G NR) to enable a mobile backhaul infrastructure. Over time, the development of mobile IAB has progressed through multiple evolutionary phases, supported by standardized protocols. This work provides a concise overview of the history driving mobile IAB advancement, examining key challenges and use cases while highlighting KPIs and performance metrics. It begins by defining the architecture and operational principles of 5G NR IAB, then explores the specific requirements and high-level mobility models for mobile IAB. The study also addresses KPIs and testing methodologies, with a detailed analysis of KPI-driven challenges—including performance degradation caused by handover and potential issues with one-way delays in uplink data transmission—before concluding on the roadmap for future research and development in mobile IAB systems.

This paper addresses the critical challenge of optimizing hyperparameters in Global Sensitivity Analysis-based sensitivity testing within the context of Sensitivity Testing. Specifically, the work aims to identify the most impactful hyperparameters for S-Test in Variational Autoencoders (VAEs), a task that proves both complex and elusive. We conduct a comprehensive review of existing VAE architectures and their associated hyperparameters, evaluating them through a S-Test experiment. By applying Global Sensitivity Analysis methodologies, we clarify the functional role of each parameter and quantify its specific influence on the model's performance outcomes. Our primary objective is to furnish researchers with a solid foundation for the systematic and informed selection of VAE hyperparameters, thereby rendering informed decisions regarding these configurations and their anticipated impact on model behavior.

We present comprehensive reasons supporting the inclusion of the wave equation within quantum mechanics, particularly emphasizing that both the wave equation itself and the associated time-dependent energy conservation principle must adhere to Lorentz invariance, requiring special relative transformations when the position is considered.

Liger is the proposed successor to the Very Wide Field Survey Camera (Wisep) at the Keck Observatory, aiming for a high-speed wide-field spectrographic capability. Its innovative three-dimensional spectroscopy design utilizes a single laser-driven gas jet to create a continuously focused line spectrum across the camera's field of view; as light traverses the imaging detector, it appears stretched along the cross-dispersion axis, forming bright source profiles known as "spectrotracks." Although these tracks can be analyzed individually, their collective utility for scientific inquiry requires reconstruction of the original data state prior to distortion. Consequently, a specialized spectrodata analysis system has been established to generate spectra from these tracks. This article details the architecture of said system, which employs a dedicated detector processing pipeline coupled with higher-level utilities capable of generating both individual and specialized data products. Furthermore, it addresses a significant shift towards generating real-time outputs and explores the associated technical obstacles, specifically within the context of modifying the Keck Observing System to accommodate Liger-specific data.

This paper introduces a new class of non-trivial, time-independent solutions in the flow domain of the two-dimensional (2D) incompressible, bounded, and periodic Navier–Stokes equations. These solutions are generated via the 2D operator theory combined with small perturbations around a base Couette flow state in the given operator framework. However, the study reveals that for the 2D operator framework to support these solutions combined with slight perturbations, they must be time-independent, time-invariant solutions of the fluid dynamic system around a base 2D operator Couette flow state in the field theory of 2D incompressible, bounded and periodic Euler equations. These solutions of the fluid system are identified as complex traveling wave structures that integrate spatial phase shifts into their core definition, integrating spatial phase shifts into their core definition. These solutions exhibit properties analogous to wave packets in higher-energy physics, such as the possibility of localization within momentum space and the presence of a de Broglier wavelength that links classical and quantum mechanical descriptions of matter waves through the Heisenberg uncertainty principle which underpins many modern physics theories including string theory and loop quantum gravity models developed over centuries by generations of scientists around the world.

We illustrate the demonstration of full optical linear polarization control within individual and interacting condensates arising from exciton-polariton decay. This achievement stems from a intricate interaction framework that enables in-phase and out-of-phase coupling between the spin components of these components. As a result, we realize a tunable state with a specifically defined phase offset between the two components of this framework. We analyze the resulting inter-component interference to precisely explain the mechanism behind this specific phase relationship. Ultimately, these phenomena position spin engineering via exciton-polariton interactions as a potent method for exploring multicomponent quantum phenomena and creating advanced optical devices.

This paper examines how to leverage data for addressing and forecasting the COVID-19 outbreak in South Africa. We first highlight the critical role of integrated, well-organized datasets in crisis response and outline methods to incorporate them into data-driven models designed to project viral spread and assess healthcare requirements. Furthermore, we propose techniques for enhancing existing statistics through the application of web-scraping and the analysis of freely available information from e-government portals. Concluding with a discussion on leveraging mobile phone positioning data to refine outbreak models, we illustrate these approaches using a case study focused on a COVID-19 model developed for South Africa.

We strengthen Freiman's 3k-4 theorem by demonstrating that if the cardinality of the difference set $|A-A|$ in a finite integer set $A$ satisfies the inequality $\frac{5}{3}|A| \leq |A-A| < 3k-4$ , then their arithmetic progression structure must be $A = \left[ (3k-4-d)+x \mid x \in P \right] \cup Q$, where $d \in \mathbb{N}$ is such that $0 \leq d \leq |A|-1$, and both $P$ and $Q$ constitute integer sets with cardinalities at least $|A|-d$. This result generalizes existing findings showing that under certain sumset cardinality constraints, finite integer sets can be expressed as the union of an arithmetic progression of cardinality at most the original set minus one and a "small" co-cardinality integer set. Our findings also generalize to scenarios where differences are constrained within specific density ranges rather than specific upper bounds, thereby broadening the scope of known results in additive combinatorics.

Medical imaging is frequently employed in the analysis, diagnosis, and management of chronic disorders such as diabetic retinopathy and glaucoma. Although these conditions primarily affect the retina and involve distinct diagnostic procedures, a shared preliminary step often exists: both conditions typically begin with retinal non-perfusion. This study specifically examines diabetic gradation via fundus photographs and glaucoma assessment using optic disc imagery. We utilize state-of-the-art deep learning models to classify each condition independently, extracting features from 480×480 pixel images to generate a common structural representation. These unified features are subsequently evaluated using machine learning classifiers to determine the efficacy of this fusion strategy. The findings reveal that integrating both information sources surpasses the performance of using data modals in isolation, yielding an AUC of 0.9225.

X-ray imaging serves as a primary diagnostic method for identifying infections in the general population, particularly in resource-limited settings lacking advanced technologies for detecting Inflammatory markers (IRs). However, the current literature reveals significant gaps in understanding the radiographic characteristics specific to Coronavirus disease-2019. The proposed paper examines these potential indicators within X-ray images by analyzing clinical data sets from the Eastern Mediterranean, specifically Northeast Africa, utilizing images acquired from three distinct hospitals. The visual inspection highlights several key areas for further investigation: (i) asymmetrical involvement of lung fields, (ii) bilateral or localized patterns with greater frequency in the lower lung zones, (iii) an elevated ratio of opacity to lung volume compared to the non-infected, (iv) markers indicating a more advanced stage of pulmonary involvement, and (v) signs suggesting that the course of illness is more prolonged among infected individuals than in uninfected individuals. The current study's visual inspection indicates a promising foundation for future research, particularly the development of machine-learning models capable of quantifying these indicators to enhance the diagnosis of Coronavirus disease-2019.

We examine the one-dimensional idealization of light scattering within spherically stratized materials, focusing on cases where properties such as impedance or refractive index change increasingly sharply. A key observation is that transmission eigenfunctions associated with eigenvalues approaching infinity become confined, or "localized," near the outer boundary of the domain. Depending on how impedances are arranged relative to one another, this implies either that all spherical Bessel function coefficients in an expansion become negligible except for a finite number as n increases, or alternatively, that all coefficients for external modes outside the medium vanish in the asymptotic limit. These findings align with and support prior results derived using asymptotic methods.

In speech recognition and natural language processing, intent recognition is a critical task with numerous real-world applications. Current approaches typically depend heavily on large datasets of annotated utterances, creating significant barriers to entry due to the challenges of data collection and the high costs associated with annotation. To address these limitations, this paper introduces a novel method for intent discovery designed to function with limited training data by leveraging the implicit relationships between different intents. Specifically, we employ a pre-training and contrastive learning framework to establish a semantic framework for intents, thereby enhancing the performance of intent recognition models on unseen classes. Extensive experiments conducted across two benchmark datasets confirm that our proposed approach achieves state-of-the-art performance.

This study re-examines the Adler-Bobenko-Suris H₂ equation through a correspondence involving linear relationships to $S^{(0,0)}$ and $S^{(1,0)}$ variables within the Cauchy matrix hierarchy. We analyze the coupled quad-system associated with distinct expressions of these variables and validate the six-point self-adjointness property specifically for the $S^{(0,0)}$ component.

This paper investigates the challenge of visual relationship detection alongside strategies for mitigating the high false positive rate characteristic of current best solutions, such as inaccurate object and attribute predictions. We propose a novel method for relationship verification, which demonstrates a 10% relative reduction in false positives on the recent COCO-Objects-at-Home benchmark. A metric named quantum correlation cost (QCC) is introduced to evaluate discord-like correlations within or among any set of multiple quantum systems. The QCC represents the minimal total correlation discrepancy among the systems resulting from a non-demoting projective measurement. The study further explores the relationship between QCC and various measurements that are neither fully strong nor fully weak. Findings reveal two key points: first, the QCC remains invariant under arbitrary strong projective measurements performed on the complement of the measurement target; second, the QCC achieves its maximum value when the non-demoting measurement is completely dispersed across all possible outcomes (i.e., conducted as a completely weak measurement). These discoveries establish a optimal quantum correlation cost for the weak measurement and clarify the connection between the QCC and the operational definition of quantum correlation strength (QCS).

Extracting relationships from unstructured text is crucial for building knowledge graphs, yet existing methods face challenges: neural approaches fail to leverage the structural benefits of parsers, past graph neural networks depend on manual feature selection, and they treat relationship extraction as isolated instances. Addressing these limitations, this paper introduces iSTEG, an finishing inference end-to-end framework initialized from first principles. This model integrates a graph neural network with a transformer-based encoder to handle textual input, systematically relationship-pair identification, and semantic consistency verification within generated relation lists. Specifically, it employs GN to capture structural characteristics of relation sets, uses TN to highlight semantic traits in the provided context, and applies a combined scoring mechanism to filter out inconsistent output pair candidates. Demonstrated on the FAIG dataset (version F. A), the "iSTEG" model significantly surpasses traditional baselines while reducing development efforts related to feature engineering.

While deep neural networks dominate modern computer vision, they frequently fail to capitalize on two critical prior knowledge areas: spatial and hierarchical structures within visual data. Although recurrent networks have historically addressed sequence structures, convolutional networks remain the standard for visual recognition tasks, largely ignoring both temporal evolution and the formation of higher-level structures from lower components. We introduce Dynamic Graph Message Passing Networks (DGMPN) to enforce both spatial and hierarchical model capacity. First, we enable networks to learn adaptive graph structures for specific visual recognition tasks, capitalizing on the inherent spatial relationships in images or batches. Building on this, we implement a recursive hierarchy where low-level graph messages are aggregated to construct progressively higher-level graphs, thereby mirroring natural multi-scale structure. We demonstrate that this dual approach significantly boosts performance: in scene parsing, DGMPN exceeds current state-of-the-art results despite using less capacity; in object detection, it achieves state-of-the-art accuracy and current leading methodologies fail to fully explain its success. These results confirm that explicitly incorporating spatial and hierarchical knowledge enhances both efficiency and effectiveness, while the architecture itself offers the most plausible explanation for these unexpected performance gains.

Multiple Constant Multiplication (MCM) is critical for efficient hardware implementation, especially when dealing with floating-point operations. Typically, MCM techniques involve expressing a product as a series of additions and subtractions, where the goal is often to minimize the count of required 4-to-1 multiplexers. While the 2's complement method is standard, it frequently demands a high volume of multiplexers. This study introduces a novel algorithm that significantly reduces both the operation cost (in terms of logic elements) and multiplexer count. By exemplarily applying the proposed approach alongside other contemporary methods for calculating the natural logarithm, the analysis evaluates the results and compares them against 2's complement and binary reflected coded (BRC) multiplication strategies.

Quantum deep learning investigates integrating quantum computing methods with deep neural networks. Although these two fields evolved independently for years, the realization that quantum circuits can mimic artificial neural networks sparked their widespread adoption. This paper outlines the fundamental principles and historical context of quantum deep learning, highlights significant milestones, examines the multifaceted challenges within the research, and finally proposes promising future research directions and potential application areas.

Radio frequency (RF) acceleration technologies are fundamental to contemporary and future high-energy particle colliders, and this paper outlines the status of their research and development as reported to the American Snowmass meeting in 2021. With this foundational context, we examine various prospective projects and opportunities for advancing RF accelerator tech across four primary areas: (a) Superconducting Radio Frequency (SRF) systems, including high-field applications; (b) Accelerating structures designed for compactness; (c) Normal-conducting RF systems aimed at high power and efficiency; and (stray) magnetic-based driving structures. Finally, we conclude by reviewing the advanced RF driver electronics and their development.

Physicians have long been interested in discovering the new heavy particle discovered at the LHC, specifically by creating it again through the s-channel using more energetic muon-antimutation collisions. Since the proposed 3- or 6-Tev muon collider could clarify the properties and nature of this event, it represents an attractive option for the next-generation high-energy physics facility. However, this endeavor faces major difficulties, primarily the very short lifetime of muons, which necessitates sophisticated ring design strategies to compensate. These difficulties have historically delayed the project, though recent efforts have made significant strides toward a realistic feasibility study. This presentation examines both the high physical potentials and the operational obstacles associated with the muon collider initiative.

We analyze the dispersion relations of linearized perturbations—specifically scalar, vector, and tensor modes—for a viscous relativistic fluid governed by a generalized framework (extending Navier-Stokes equations) that remains compliant with the causal principle. Within this study, we determine the dispersion relations for a fluid in thermal equilibrium moving with constant velocity, considering scenarios both with and without viscosity. Our findings reveal that, regardless of the viscous context, the phase velocity of perturbations aligns with the fluid's flow velocity.

This study calculates the isotropic background of gamma-ray photons from primordial black holes (PBHs) formed during the early universe within specific theoretical frameworks, specifically evaluating their potential impact on future CMB-S4 observational projects. The results indicate that even a minuscule fraction of the dark matter—less than $10^{-11}$ fractions—composed of PBHs with masses situated between $10^{15}$ and $3\times 10^{16} \, \text{ev}$ would be detectable under these circumstances. The analysis specifically examines two formation scenarios: direct formation through thermal fluctuations of the inflaton and post-inflation production via annihilation of magnetic monopots at the Planck mass scale (TMBH model). In the latter scenario involving TMBHs, the resulting gamma-ray flux could be enhanced by orders of magnitude relative to other predictions, thereby influencing future experimental outlooks.

Secure multi-party computation protocols enable trusted collaboration among parties by letting them jointly analyze datasets without disclosing their private inputs. While general-purpose frameworks like mLDPC-based protocols theoretically support this, they demand immense communication overhead, often termed a "communication bottleneck," rendering them unfeasible for real-time applications such as locating missing individuals or predicting outcomes in advanced analytics, where data privacy is imperative. To address these challenges, we propose VSP—a new full-stack architecture termed the Virtual Secure Platform built upon Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) and the BGV variant, specifically tailored to accelerate real-time secure operations. Designed around a simplified, five-stage custom pipelined processor, this system eliminates inter-cpu text transfers by utilizing single-cpu local FGT and optimizing logic to minimize latency relative to standard classical applications. To ensure custom hardware designs meet the rigorous demands of decryption-free, high-throughput processing, we developed comprehensive design guidelines that harmonize classical principles with unique VSP requirements. We benchmark the system's efficacy in four practical applications—namely, a missing person detector using facial recognition with real-time video feeds; an interactive "20 Questions" game facilitating private participation; secure matrix multiplication; and secure k-nearest neighbor (kNN) classification for locating similar users. To demonstrate broad applicability, we also discuss how VSP could secure data processing within the Internet of Vehicles (IoV) to support private interactions, such as those in carpooling scenarios.

While Courcelle and others demonstrated that every language-bounded structure defines a problem with a parameterized approximation scheme (ptas) when weighted by the number of constraints, this result does not necessarily apply to problems defined by unbounded valuations. This research introduces a ptas for sparse general-valued structures that are reference-point positive with respect to some positive valued function. The algorithm extends the approach developed by Bulatov and Villanger for sparse positive relational structures and builds upon recent work by Khot, Knuth-Tarjan, and colleagues on positive-partial-order-logic definable structures. The resulting framework also provides a comprehensive study of the Fine-Grained complexity of local consistency checks. The fine analysis reveals two distinct scenarios for CSPs involving a positive partial-order-logic (pp-logic) reference point and those concerning the more complex sparse point-free CSPs with respect to it. The study shows the former case is NP-complete but solvable in sub-exponential time via an algorithm with a ptas that runs in time $2^{O(n)}$. The latter reveals an interesting split in complexity: the time requirements are linear for certain relations and cubic for others, with these findings also having significant implications for sparse CSPs with a bounded number of relations but arbitrary arities.

Pre-trained language models are capable of capturing extensive linguistic patterns from large textual datasets. Leveraging this ability without additional training, these models enable the development of powerful natural language processing systems. This utility applies particularly to syntactic parsing, where such assistance helps construct accurate analysis even in the absence of specialized supervision. This study introduces a new approach extracting parse trees by adapting the self-attention mechanisms already embedded in pre-trained architectures. By simply querying a model, one can generate dependency or constitutive parse structures using just the output layers, with no fine-tuning required. We demonstrate statistically that this technique rivals established parsers trained on standard gold standards, with generated accuracies reaching close to those of fine-tuned counterparts in specific parsing domains. Additionally, we investigate how data-sparse conditions impact performance and assess the portability of these capabilities across diverse linguistic environments, including languages with limited pre-training corpora.

High-resolution hyperspectral images (HSIs) capture spectral data across numerous bands, enabling the precise identification of materials and fine structures. Leveraging this capability, this study aims to enhance semantic segmentation for urban environments through a robust, robustly supervised approach. We acknowledge that while label creation for pixel-level segmentation is labor-intensive and impractical for vast cityscapes, the abundant detail within our HSI data offers a viable alternative. By analyzing the intrinsic properties of these images, we introduce two novel strategies: 1) generating coarse functional categories by clustering highly discriminatory spectra, and 2) producing rough mask approximations by segmenting distinct spectral clusters. These methods are evaluated on the Split-60 cityscape dataset, demonstrating performance on par with pixel-wise supervised baselines yet requiring significantly reduced annotation effort.

This study investigates the stellar activity cycles and structural changes in cool stars by analyzing simultaneous photometric and spectroscopic data for three sub-solar mass objects with effective temperatures below 5000 K: the red dwarf AD Leo, which is near the main sequence, and two sub-super giants, HD 45364 and HD 60532. All three stars possess large spots and significant rotationally induced variability. By comparing observed ratios of lithium, sodium, and chromospheric activity indices to predictions from standard Skumanich and Mamajek models, we find that only AD Leo aligns with age-dependent evolutionary expectations. In contrast, the other two stars exhibit activity levels suggesting ages orders of magnitude younger than their actual ages by at least a factor. To explain this anomalous activity, we hypothesize that both AD Leo and HD 45364 are accreting material from a companion planet located within the star's surface density scale height. This process would re-heat the star, simultaneously extending the planetary orbit and increasing its own spin rate.

The classical RAM model, constrained to only additive operations, allows execution within O(1) time for comparisons and calculations of products or factors only under specific, restrictive conditions. By introducing multiplicative comparisons to this limited RAM, we identify exactly which further O(1)-time arithmetic operations become viable under unique circumstances. Our analysis reveals a specific constraint: both integer multiplication and division are reducible to O(1)-multiplicative algorithms if and only if the machine memory size is limited to O(log n) words—precisely the space required to store polynomials of degree n over Z_2. While this model clearly supports comparisons only under distinct uniqueness conditions, our primary finding establishes that both integer multiplication and division can be performed in O(1)-time if the data set includes any n^2 variation or any other nontrivial input. Furthermore, by incorporating comparison capabilities alongside multiplicative comparisons, we demonstrate that all comparisons can ultimately be performed under any memory size condition, provided the machine supports these two comparison types simultaneously and under unique individual comparisons.

Session-based recommendations address a pivotal challenge in recommender systems involving massive e-commerce traffic. Recent deep learning advancements utilize extensive user-item interaction data to construct sophisticated session representations for accurate next-item prediction. However, many items lack sufficient historical interactions. We address this gap by employing self-supervised graph-based learning to leverage both item and user correlations, even for items with sparse session data. Building on the observation that sessions can be modeled as graphs where nodes are items and edges represent joint appearances, we introduce self-supervised graph-based methods that harness high-dimensional node features to generate robust session embeddings through supervised and self-supervised learning. Since these approaches depend on labeled or supervised data—which is often scarce—we integrate them with conventional recommender algorithms as part of a graph-based co-training framework. Experimental results across three real-world datasets confirm that our proposed framework consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines.

This paper provides a comprehensive study on linear complementary dual (LCD) codes within the framework of the linear space formed by a finite group $G$ over the field $\mathbb{F}_q$, specifically denoted as $(G, \mathbb{F}_q)$ or $LG$. We establish that $G$ admits an LCD structure if the center of the group, $\ Z(G)$, is trivial. Furthermore, by analyzing the properties of this space to derive both necessary and sufficient conditions, we locate several examples of newly defined group-specific and group-reversible LCD codes.

We investigate differential forms within an algebraic compactification of moduli spaces of metric graphs, generating canonical examples by considering the graph itself and its Jacobian. A primary finding is the application of period integrals of differential forms to generalize previous findings by Eynard and Ortiz regarding double and triple graphs. Furthermore, we demonstrate a connection between the periodicity of metric graphs and an algebraic framework by finding that the period matrix of a specific triple graph construction is none other than the metric from a relevant graph complex. This leads to proving homological properties for differential forms on these metric graphs and establishing an explicit link between the differential forms governing graph complexes and Maltcev completion.

Although recurrent neural networks (RNNs) excel in object categorization, tracking visual categories over time, information how feature flows through these architectures remains poorly understood. This study examines such data movement in trained CNN-RNN hybrids by analyzing category-orthogonal characteristics that facilitate data transmission. The authors find category-orthogonal traits initially emerge as random noise but gradually adopt object-related properties during training, with their influence on the network's performance remaining minimal. Furthermore, these non-categorical attributes serve as an efficient source of information for learning new object categories. Ultimately, such dimensions facilitate the rapid integration of fresh object attributes, like texture, into the network's object representation by decoupling this texture data from categorical information.

This paper explores how correlations influence one-dimensional non-Hermitian systems featuring point-gap topology, a phenomenon experimentally accessible through measurement of fermionic occupations. We analyze a model with point-gap topology in the absence of correlations, demonstrating that inserting correlations—a hallmark of bosonic systems—fills the resulting point gap. Surprisingly, a rich spectrum of spectral phases emerges on the "spectral edge," characterized by alternating signs in two-point spectral functions. We argue this alternation serves as a robust signature for detecting spectral edges driven by correlations, even if full characterization remains elusive. Ultimately, our findings provide essential insight into experimenting with point-gap topology in bosonic platforms.

Recently, research into multidimensional Golay complementary arrays (GCA) has surged, finding applications in beamforming for 4D synthetic aperture imaging. This study presents novel constructions for generating GCA that are simultaneously null in range and range-Doppler planes. While established methods rely on Golay complementary sequences (GCS) paired with unimodular sequences (UCS), our approach builds GCAs solely from GCS, effectively expanding the inventory of available structures. Specifically, we introduce general methods to produce Gr–DrD $\alpha$-balanced double sequences (GrDrD $\alpha$-bDS) free of UCS; from these, GCA can be derived. Our framework covers all cases where the range resolution step ($L$) is a prime number or composite ($l_1l_2$), supporting arbitrary Doppler resolution units ($M$). Although current direct methods yield single-sideband GCAs, utilizing single-sideband filters to create full-sideband arrays offers promising avenues for investigating performance-related properties like sidelobe levels and maximum peak levels alongside further developments. Maximum peak level reductions may be achievable through the combination of our proposed GCAs with other existing designs.

This study examines on-shell and off-shell Higgs boson production leading to four leptons, leveraging CMS dataset collected at the LHC during 2011, 2012, and 2013 (53 fb$^{-1}$). By analyzing this data alongside simulations of signal events and backgrounds, we estimate the total width of the Higgs boson directly from its coupling strengths and production rates as $\Gamma(H \to ZZ^*) = (5.3^{+1.0}_{-1.1})$ GeV. Assuming a Standard Model couplings structure for the Higgs, these findings also constrain deviations in the $H\to ZZ$ production cross-section from standard theory to the range $0.6 < \frac{m_H^2}{4} < 1.6$.

Detecting binary changes between co-registered hyperspectral images is crucial for monitoring the environment, with numerous practical applications driving significant research interest. This work presents a novel supervised (change classification) deep learning framework that requires access to ground truth labels but significantly reduces dependency on them by simultaneously leveraging both input change maps and spectral data. Implemented as a feature fusion autoencoder, a novel architecture designed to identify discontinuities within both spatial and spectral domains serves as its foundation. By integrating these multimodal data sources during the latent representation stage, substantial improvements are achieved in enhancing the representational capacity for change identification. Extensive testing on two datasets, the RSCC and the change-enriched subset of the RSUE, confirms that this new method substantially outperforms state-of-the-art benchmarks and existing upper limits of accuracy. Specifically, on the RSCC, a pixel-wise accuracy of 88.2% and an F1 score of 87.9% are achieved, effectively approaching theoretical performance ceilings. Similarly, results obtained from the complex spectral variations in the change-enriched subset of the RSUE demonstrate sustained high-level accuracy.

Quantum tunneling between silicon atoms enables coherent coupling across multiple quantum dots, opening pathways for rich system-specific phenomena. In this study, we utilize a scanning tunneling microscope to exchange two electrons on individual silicon atoms within a crystal's quantum lattice. The two in-system energy valleys undergo interference as the phase relationship varies between atoms under low electronic contact resistance conditions, producing a characteristic "anti-bonding" feature known as the Kondo anti-bond state (RPS). Furthermore, we observe that as the distance between atoms increases, the correlation strength among three atoms increases while valence interference effects diminish due to weak coupling in system-limited regimes (RPS). These observations provide direct visualization of valley interference combined with RPS, contributing to a deeper understanding of silicon-based quantum devices.

Optimization methods serve as essential tools across numerous scientific and commercial fields, enabling effective solutions to complex issues. Consequently, researchers continually develop novel optimization strategies to enhance problem-solving capabilities. However, existing software often employs conservative design principles, which can hinder the rapid development, testing, and deployment of innovative and cutting-edge techniques. To address this limitation, we present LibOPT: a highly modular open-source software suite written in C++14 and 11 dedicated to solving continuous optimization problems. This framework supports a wide variety of modern methods, including those that are state-of-the-art as well as emerging innovations. Additionally, it offers tools for implementing and developing new algorithms, and its extensive scope makes it suitable for tackling diverse practical applications in research and industry.

We present a systematic analysis comparing the properties of non-commutative particles on plans derived from both the Moyal deformation and the fuzzy sphere models. This work demonstrates that the inherent non-commutativity in these frameworks leads to modifications in physical properties, specifically altering the particles' dispersion relations and state density while leaving the system's thermodynamics essentially unchanged.

The rise of toxic content on social media platforms—including hate speech, offensive language, and misogyny—poses significant challenges to our societies. While much of the research addressing this issue has concentrated on class-based tasks, such identification requires a nuanced understanding of the underlying context, which also enables categorization into sub-types of misogyny. To achieve this dual functionality simultaneously, which benefits model performance by leveraging shared patterns across datasets, we introduce a deep multi-task model. Specifically tailored to identify and classify misogyny within Arabic social media content, which is a critical area currently lacking resources, we note that contextual analysis has often been underexploored in previous studies. Experiments conducted on two datasets demonstrate the model's superior performance, achieving an F1-score of 89.99\% for misogyyny identification and 82.19\% for categorization, while further semantic analysis provides insights into the learned representations within our approach, which extends to broader applications in identifying abusive and harmful online content.

This paper explores the solvability of specific types of fractional backward stochastic differential equations (BSDEs) that include delayed generators within their framework. These equations are defined over a closed time interval $[0,T]$. Their dynamics rely on the history of the driving Brownian motion within the period $[0,t]$. Specifically, they consider scenarios where both the drift ($f$) and diffusion ($h$) functions depend not only on current states but also on trajectories over the past $[t_0,t]$. 

In their theoretical analysis, they employ the 1-Riesz measure framework alongside assumptions regarding b-modes (bounded mean-difference inequalities) for $f$ and $h$, which assure joint continuity along with growth constraints for these functions dependent on prior $[0,t_0]$. They ultimately prove the existence and uniqueness of solutions while deriving growth constraints for these solutions based on the constraints imposed by the $f$ and $h$ functions. These findings demonstrate that assuming growth constraints for equations' free terms $f, h, g$ allows for establishing corresponding constraints on the resulting processes $Y$ and $\chi$. Specifically, they show that if linear growth constraints are imposed for $f, h, g$, then $Y$ and $\chi$ will satisfy similar constraints; if quadratic growth constraints are imposed for $f, h, g$, then $Y$ and $\chi$ will satisfy analogous constraints.

Model-based reinforcement learning aims to approximate an optimal policy by learning a world model that estimates the true environment, often yielding superior sample efficiency compared to model-free approaches. This study investigates the robustness and generalization capabilities of policies developed through this framework under slight environmental changes, drawing inspiration from the probabilistic PILCO method. We introduce regularization for policy optimization and more robust control agents through the enforcement of lower bounds on likelihood variance within the Gaussian Process dynamics model, with empirical evidence supporting the approach's efficacy in simulation tests.

Various networking challenges, including coded caching distribution, network storage, and coded computing, have significant potential to enhance current communication systems. Motivated by this, this research seeks to establish a unified framework capable of modeling diverse coding strategies for these problems. Presented here is a proposed framework—capable of representing the most comprehensive scenario—along with an analysis of the associated distribution strategies. We investigate methodological details such as file selection, matrix choices, and coefficient vector determination, examining how these components influence system performance from both the system perspective and the source/files perspective. The study concludes by highlighting the framework's versatility in addressing issues like caching distribution and storing data within distributed distributed storage systems.

We develop the univalent type theory model of PCF featuring univalence, higher inductive types, higher induction, and higher recursiveness. This construction yields the initial algebra for the functor $X \mapsto \mathbb{N} \times (X + (X \to X))$. Given the presence of univalence and higher induction within the system, the models of higher PCU can be characterized through the lens of 1-truncated simplicities. Specifically, there is an equivalence between type-theoretic constructions and higher categorical structures, namely 2-truncated simplicities, subject to additional constraints.

This paper investigates the precise pole structure of automorphic Langlands Eisenstein series for $GL(n,\mathbb{A}_\mathbb{Q})$. The resulting description of these poles arises from a novel combinatorial formulation of the arithmetic contribution during their reduction to purely local terms at infinity.

This study addresses safe control challenges within mobile robotic systems operating among dynamic obstacles on uneven ground. To guarantee safety, we integrate configuration-aware barriers into the mobile robot's configuration-space obstacle regions by constructing specific barrier functions. These functions are formulated to respect the kinematic constraints of the robot and explicitly account for its dynamics, including position, orientation, angular velocity, and velocities of the end-effectors. Subsequently, we derive a configuration-aware barrier function by synthesizing these individual barriers through an algebraic technique. Finally, we develop a configuration-aware safe controller by merging a configuration-aware barrier function with a time-optimal controller. The proposed method is evaluated via simulations featuring a mobile platform navigating a challenging, uneven terrain while carrying a 7-DOF arm and avoiding collisions with two obstacles moving at random.

Natural language processing is a critical academic area focused on comprehending digital text, a process frequently hindered by inadequate digital representations arising from the wide variety of human speech patterns. This paper investigates specific graph algorithms to address text summarization through an extractive approach. To evaluate sentence resemblance, two metrics are examined: overlap in sentence overlap distance, and edit distance between sentences .

While Bose-Einstein condensates (BECs) have been extensively researched in quantum information science, this study advances the proposal of utilizing quantum optics to generate nonlinear quantum gates. We present a rigorous theoretical analysis showing that integrating optical trapping with suitable couplings can induce a nonlinearity within the many-body quantum state of a RBEC. This induced nonlinearity, implemented through a feasible optical mechanism, enables the realization of fundamental single-qubit quantum gates. This approach offers a promising and ground-breaking technique for quantum optics and information processing.

Digital vector lines, such as those found in map features like roads and rivers, frequently encounter discontinuities due to changes in geometry or attribute. Standard rendering methods for these vectors fail to look realistic at close viewing distances because they lack smooth joins at discontinuities. While prior research has addressed aesthetic joins for 3D models, extending this to 2D vector maps presents specific technical hurdles, notably a susceptibility to visual artifacts like aliasing and noticeable performance drops. To overcome these issues, this paper introduces a novel anti-aliasing approach that provides smooth vector renders with efficient, anti-aliasing treatment at discontinuous points.

Multiquadric quasi-interpolation via univariate quasi-interpolation operators has historically struggled to retain shapes due to the non-monotonicity inherent in its bandwidth parameter. This study introduces a novel quasicounterpart quADF function that serves as a solution by ensuring global monotonicity and preserving shapes. We prove C1 smoothness for this operator and establish an approximation result showing that the proposed method achieves first-order convergence.

Pulsar halos, defined as a newly identified class of extended gamma-ray sources, consist of photon emission occurring approximately 300 parsecs from the pulsar center. These regions are produced by cosmic-ray electrons and positrons injected into the radiation-dominated relativistic wind sphere of pulsars. Due to their proximity to pulsars, pulsar halos are considered significant components of the Galaxy's positron positron source. However, the formation of these regions depends on specific environmental conditions, such as the presence of a low-density pulsar wind. This paper reviews recent observations and predictions regarding pulsar halos, with a focus on the most prominent examples: the nearby death-bed Crab Nebula and the Tarantula Nebula (Tarantula) Spider.

Adverse weather conditions significantly impact human activities, vehicle operations, and transportation systems. While various automatic systems depend on visual imagery to detect such conditions, current methods based on image convolutional neural networks (CNNs) are limited because they were trained on existing datasets and thus only perform optimally for those specific sets. This limitation has led researchers to suggest that these methods would benefit from a CNN model capable of handling a broader range of weather types. In this paper, we first present the first multi-class weather dataset, which is publicly available on the internet. This dataset comprises 1,500 manually selected color images for each condition (sunny, cloudy, rainy, and misty/foggy), resulting in a total of 6,000 labeled images. A comprehensive analysis of various Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) models for four-way classification tasks is provided in this study. We observe that the best results are achieved by ResNet50 when image augmentation is applied to the input datasets, yielding an accuracy of 89.99% and the AUC score of 88.33%.

We examine how how people form beliefs about climate change by integrating scientific data within their specific institutional settings, using a basic economic model. The study shows that when the rate of information flow from scientists to the public is low, public belief diverges from actual reality; when this belief falls short of scientific consensus, individuals will not adopt actions—such as reducing carbon emissions—to address climate change. However, these discrepancies between public perception and scientific reality can be minimized when people have a foundational understanding of how those public beliefs work. Ultimately, creating effective communication channels to share information about climate change is crucial for ensuring the public forms accurate beliefs and addresses the issue accordingly.

Soft grippers have gained significant attention due to their ability to securely grasp diverse and fragile objects. However, their complex nonlinear dynamics and susceptibility to disturbances often lead to grasps that are inconsistent, inaccurate, or unstable. To address these challenges, this paper introduces an affordable, data-driven approach that enables the precise and stable control of multi-finger soft actuators. The core mechanism employs a multispectral model-based controller, where non-linear dynamic behaviors are approximated using linear models identified online via Koopman operator theory, relying on sparse sensor data. By integrating these models with a multi-finger trajectory planner, we achieve precise online adaptation even amidst significant variations in payloads or environmental conditions. Optimization strategies are pivotal in machine learning, influencing both optimality results and computational feasibility. A prime example is Gradient Descent (GD), which has established robust theoretical bounds regarding convergence speed and solution quality. In contrast, Natural Gradient Descent (NGD) offers superior performance for specific domains, yet generalization of GD-style bounds to NGD within the broader context has been lacking. This work introduces a novel framework that extends key properties of standard gradient descent—specifically ensuring linearity and exactness of the gradient projection—to NGD. By utilizing this extension, we derive novel proofs for property preservation under coordinate transformations and perturbed gradients for NGD. These techniques yield novel bounds for the convergence rate and solution sub-optimality in strongly convex settings where noise is present, applying to linear elastic net, matrix elastic net, and softmax regression tasks. Experimentally, these new bounds align closely with empirical observations.

This study introduces a multimodal machine learning model designed to predict outcomes in patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). As the most prevalent lung cancer subtype, NSCLC treatments are guided by a blend of clinical data and imaging analyses, yet prior attempts at building prognosis-specific prediction models have yielded limited success. Our approach integrates heterogeneous data sources—specifically tabular clinical records and radiological images—to leverage synergistic patterns for patient outcome forecasting. For the image component, we employ transfer learning using the pre-trained ResNet50 architecture, fine-tuned on our dataset alongside two advanced tabular algorithms: XGBoost and a Long Short-Term Neural Network (LSTM). The proposed method is evaluated on a cohort of 852 patients with matched pre-treatment images and clinical information. Experimental results indicate strong performance for our ResNet50 and LSTM algorithms, achieving concordance indices of 0.700 and 0.685, respectively, with results matching those of the tested XGBoost model. We hope this work promotes further collaboration and data sharing within the lung cancer research community.

Representing states is crucial for learning processes and agents in Reinforcement Learning. In different tasks, this representation is sometimes built from natural language or takes natural language entirely as the input form. This overview analyzes methods found in literature used for constructing natural language state representations. It advocates further for linguistically interpretable and grounded designs, demands careful justifying design decisions alongside the effectiveness evaluation across diverse approaches in both natural language processing and decision-making systems under uncertainty.

We introduce an end-to-end machine learning pipeline designed to reconstruct the power spectrum of cosmic matter density from individual quasar spectral data. By training on a substantial set of simulated data, the model successfully captures the non-linear relationship between observed spectral features and the underlying power spectrum. We then apply this trained model to observational data obtained from the SDSS/BOSS survey. The resulting power spectrum matches closely with previously published reconstructions derived via traditional tomographic techniques and specific observational observables, although the model exhibits slightly elevated error bars in the high-wavenumber domain. Ultimately, this study demonstrates the potential for adapting machine learning algorithms to large-scale astronomical datasets, thereby reducing the reliance on extensive observational data for spectrum analysis.

This study investigates specific weak modules over Weyl-type Lie algebras, focusing on the moment maps induced by these representations. It establishes the second moment map is surjective when restricted to weak high-degree modules, with kernel derived as an ideal of the representation degree. Furthermore, we identify the module as freeness and module isomorphism classifications in the case where the moment map is an injection. These findings are especially significant for $h$-free holonomic modules over Weyl algebras, where $\h$ denotes a specific hyperplane, and involve the first- and second-degree moments of this scenario.

Emotional monitoring on platforms like Twitter through sentiment analysis serves companies, as well as private parties; however, the nature of this function has made it increasingly important and challenging, requiring organizations from both sides to keep a close eye. To this effect, this paper includes a diverse of manually labeled, publicly available tweet datasets, which then provide seven sources of training content. Following this manual tagging, this work presents an novel method to analyze an historical sequence using Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) neural networks to predict the emotion of single tweets. By employing this technique with an an alternative approach to compare our proposed method with existing models, the comparison demonstrates an improved level of accuracy.

Open-ended dialogue models, trained using large-scale Language Models (LMs), have achieved significant success in creating conversational agents capable of producing human-like responses. Conversely, recent work explores incorporating LM capabilities into dialogue policy networks to allow for interactive planning and deeper understanding of complex scenarios. We introduce a new architecture that merges these two lines of research by integrating large-scale LMs directly into planning mechanisms within the dialogue policy, a development made feasible by growing training data efficiency. Our proposed framework enables detailed role-specific interactions, allowing users to engage with conversational agents in deeper, sustained roles. We evaluated this new architecture using two complex open-ended tasks: specific dialogue scenarios involving restaurant planning and medicine, alongside more traditional, open-ended tasks involving sustained dialogue with people virtual assistants. The empirical results confirm that our architecture effectively learns intricate, role-specific tasks, demonstrating superior performance in managing difficult multi-turn interactions compared to baseline models.

Gravitational wave memory refers to a permanent imprint on free-falling test masses, which, when aggregated across numerous events, may constitute part of the Stochastic Gravitational Wave Background (SGWB). This phenomenon, which cannot be replicated by any standard stochastic signal generated by traditional astrophysical compact objects, can instead provide valuable supplementary information about said signals. By analyzing the spectral characteristics of the resulting memory-based SGWB, researchers can identify its presence, thereby offering new avenues for future detection efforts using both ground-based detectors and pulsar timing arrays.

Supersymmetry (SUSY) offers a theoretically well-motivated framework to address SUSY-breaking and the associated gravitational interactions. We demonstrate that this sector provides a unified origin for three major phenomena: the large matter-antimatter asymmetry, significant gravitational wave emissions, and micro black holes, all stemming from a first-order cosmological phase transition. Our model explains matter generation through the decay of susytons—the hypothetical particle order parameter field—while gravitational waves are produced by supersonic supytons decaying into radiation during the transition. Additionally, we show that certain decays yield mini black holes, with their evaporation generating baryons that contribute to the overall asymmetry. These mechanisms collectively suggest a robust scenario where gravity waves and mini black holes serve as observable signatures supporting supersymmetry. We specifically propose an extended SUSY framework, where a complex scalar field drives a transition at the PeV energy scale, yielding a gravitational wave amplitude of $\Omega_{GW}h^2 \sim 10^{-7}$ at frequencies of $f \sim$ Hz, alongside mini black holes that generate baryons through subsequent evaporation.

Semantic communication (SC) has gained significant attention for its ability to reduce transmission bandwidth by sending only essential information characteristics. However, current SC frameworks often fail to effectively adapt to dynamic channel conditions and user demands because the sender and receiver struggle to align on which data features are most critical. This paper proposes an integrated solution to bridge that terminology and logic gap through the convergence of emergent communication, neural-symbolic reasoning, and causal inference. Specifically, we utilize signaling games to formalize the communication interaction, where the sender identifies and transmits a selection of features. These features are then processed by the receiver, who constructs a specific reasoning and causal representation based on them. To optimize sender and receiver strategies, we develop a neural-network architecture capable of learning from experience via offline reinforcement training. Furthermore, we introduce a graph-based symbolic component that enables the system to perform causal reasoning. By decoupling correlations within the sender's analysis, this architecture helps the receiver distinguish true causes from mere associations, thereby enhancing the robustness of the received decision-making processes. Extensive experimental evaluations, including real-time video analysis for the sender and subsequent decision-making for the receiver, demonstrate superior performance compared to existing methods. The results indicate that our new framework delivers more reliable communication outcomes, superior inference accuracy, and greater robustness in decision-making.

Historically, researchers have placed a strong emphasis on creating new words and predicting missing ones to enhance the effectiveness of Natural Language Processing applications, particularly in text prediction. While the introduction of Machine Learning shifted development toward model-centric strategies to address text inference, the general consensus remains that no single method emerges as universal. Since specific contexts often dictate predictive success, many current approaches integrate multiple techniques to achieve optimal performance. Consequently, the objective of hybrid models is generally to leverage the specific strengths of existing methods. The primary aim of this research is to present a novel, methodologically simple yet highly performant hybrid word model by integrating Naive Bayes algorithm characteristics with latent information. The study further analyzes how character frequencies within text influence model performance and note the influence of latent information. Experimental results, comparing these suggestions to the existing state-of-the-art, reveal that our proposed method is statistically more performant.

Recent progress in Session-based Recommendation (SB-Rank) has been fueled by self-attention mechanisms. This paper introduces SRE-KO, an efficient two-stage model, during the encoding phase which leverages a fast and effective method to generate user and session representations in an input-agnostic manner which is then used in an output prediction phase, SRE-KO is then applied to a large-scale recommendation task. Experimental results on three datasets show that SRE-KO achieves competitive performance in terms of efficiency and effectiveness compared to other state-of-the-art models.

This paper addresses collision avoidance and shape preservation within drone swarms. It introduces two primary contributions: (1) a new algorithm rooted in the Theory of Point Set Registration (TPSR) designed to prevent collisions, and (2) an adaptation weighing two centroid-based point set formation maintenance strategies. The first strategy employs a many-to-many mapping, whereas the second uses one-to-one mapping. These approaches are illustrated through two experimental scenarios involving ten quadcopters navigating an unspecified environment. The first scenario tests stationary form preservation with copter spacing at 2 meters. The second simulates dynamic movement across an undefined path. Experimental outcomes demonstrate that one many-to-one many centroid approach and two distinct one-to-one mappings achieve comparable collision avoidance performance. However, only the one-to-one configurations successfully maintain cell integrity; the many-to-many approach results in deformation.

Central to the proof is the introduction of the large $p$-core $p'$-partition number $lp(C)$, which measures the distance from an $p'$-partition $C$ to the largest $p$-core containing it. The main contribution is the demonstration of unconditional uniform distributions of $lp(C)$ within each Durfee $n$-slice, thereby generalizing prior work by Bousquet-Mloloilol (which applied only to $p=2$). These findings rely heavily on random walk models executed on graphs representing partitions by edge-removal; when restricted to specific number theory contexts for various primes, these graphs reveal first and last passage bridge numbers as well as cumulative distances from large $p$ cores. The analysis also highlights several graph structural insights, including the derivation of explicit formulas for the total number of large $p$ core $p'$-partitions and closed forms for subgraphs that cannot arise as Durфе $n$ slices.

Neural network architectures for point clouds have recently gained significant attention. To effectively train these models using neural networks, noise injection techniques known as data augmentation or smoothing are necessary. However, the most common current smoothing method, averaging stochastic points, is constrained by the points' irregular positions and fails to incorporate spatial relationships. We introduce a new augmentation approach that uses a transform-specific method to smooth point cloud datasets, enabling more robust training for these specific networks. This proposed technique outperforms existing smoothestClaps methods within a similar computational framework, which is a crucial advancement in this research area, allowing for better generalization of results. This research shows a significant improvement in both generalization and accuracy when compared to current deep learning methods for similar tasks in 3D point cloud processing, a field in rapid development since 2020.

This paper examines medium access mechanisms within sensor networks comprising Frequency Modulated Continuous Wave radars, specifically targeting collision avoidance in uplink transmissions. Focusing on two standard protocols—Slotted ALOHA and CSMA—we propose matching theoretical achievable rates for these systems under the constraint of binary output feedback. Leveraging the resulting mathematical models of each protocol, we estimate key operational parameters to optimize performance. Additionally, we contrast Slotted ALOHA and CSMA by suggesting adjustments to refine the Slotted ALOHA implementation, thereby minimizing inter-frame collisions and enhancing overall system efficiency.

Temporal Knowledge Graph Completion (TKGC) has emerged as a critical capability in diverse fields, including recommendation engines, natural language processing, and biomedical research, facilitating the inference of missing information from sparse historical data. Although existing methods have progressed, many rely on rigid architectural constraints or complex neural structures that hinder generalization and slow down training. In response, this paper proposes a framework that combines a low-rank decomposition of the relation incidence tensor with model-agnostic matrix factorization to achieve temporal relationship embeddings, which are then integrated with a neural module for entity representation learning. Beyond these core components, several strategies have been developed to enhance the model's performance through regularization, loss function improvements, and efficient batch sampling. Empirical evaluations on real-world datasets confirm the method's state-of-the-art status, while its architectural flexibility and simplicity enable training with minimal resources and foster strong generalization.

These theoretical findings were validated against finite-element method simulations and experimental data obtained from dropping steel balls of varying masses and materials (rubber and steel) onto concrete and asphalt surfaces. The results demonstrate that high-mass objects, particularly in low-impedance environments, generate ground sound predominant over modal responses, whereas lightweight objects typically produce sound patterns similar to those of breaking brittle materials governed primarily by internal modal behavior.

This study investigates amenability within arithmetic groups by examining two distinct concepts: weak and strong triviality. We establish connections linking these forms of triviality, stiffness, and weak exactness in the framework of C*-algebras and operator algebras. Specifically, we demonstrate that when $G$ is an arithmetic group satisfying Gelfand-Kazhdan relative to a suitable semisimple compact group, weak triviality of $G$ is equivalent to the stiffness of its maximal C*-algebra, providing a connection to the centralizer properties of representations. As direct results from these theoretical connections, we confirm the non-amenability of several arithmetic groups, notably showing that $\pm\Gamma\cong(\Gamma\rtimes r)$ is not amenable for any hyperbolic element $r$ in the arithmetic subgroup $\Gamma\of G(\mathbb{Q})$. We also demonstrate that the semigroup ring $L^1(\pm\Gamma)$ is not a trivial ring under certain conditions. Finally, we prove that the semigroup algebra $L^1(\Gamma\rtimes r)$ retains the amenability of its underlying group component $\Gamma$, thereby establishing that if $\Gamma\of G(\mathbb{Q})$ is a finite index subgroup of a given arithmetic group $\Gamma$, then the semigroup algebra $L^1(\Gamma\rtimes r)$ is amenability iff the group $\Gamma$ itself is amenability.

Fail-operational systems are increasingly vital in safety-critical fields, enabling safety-integrity level (SIL) 2 and SIL 3 functionalities. These systems must continue operating safely after a fault is detected, a requirement often formalized as the persistence of safe-state transitions (SST) following a fault. Unlike traditional fail-safe approaches where the system must stop during a defect, or fail-safe modes where only the system must reach a state, the fail-operational approach is unique in that the system is expected to remain functional and safe.
